name: jewish_holidays_and_fast_days
title: Jewish Holidays, Festivals, Fast Days, and Shabbat
summary: Look up the Jewish holiday, festival, fast day, or Shabbat associated with a Gregorian civil date, with optional Israel/diaspora scheduling and Hebrew or transliterated English names.

tools.name: get_jewish_holiday
tools.description: Determine whether a Gregorian date is a Jewish holiday, including both major/minor festivals and fast days, and return its name and category.

params.name: date
params.description: Gregorian civil date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

params.name: israel
params.description: Use the Israel holiday schedule when true; otherwise use the diaspora schedule.

params.name: hebrew
params.description: Return names in Hebrew letters when true; otherwise return transliterated English names.

params.name: prefix_day
params.description: Prefix multi-day festival names with the day number, such as '1 Pesach'. Fast-day names are not prefixed by the library.

returns.name: date
returns.description: The queried Gregorian date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: holiday
returns.description: Combined holiday name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a holiday.

returns.name: is_holiday
returns.description: True if the date is a Jewish holiday.

returns.name: kind
returns.description: Either 'fast_day' or 'festival' when a holiday is present, otherwise null.

returns.name: fast_day
returns.description: Fast-day name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a fast day.

returns.name: is_fast_day
returns.description: True if the date is a fast day.

returns.name: festival
returns.description: Festival name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a festival.

returns.name: is_festival
returns.description: True if the date is a festival.

tools.implementation_notes: Parse the YYYY-MM-DD string into integers and construct `date_obj = GregorianDate(year, month, day)` from `pyluach.dates`. Import `fast_day`, `festival`, and `holiday` from `pyluach.hebrewcal`. Call `fast_name = fast_day(date_obj, hebrew=hebrew)`, `festival_name = festival(date_obj, israel=israel, hebrew=hebrew, include_working_days=True, prefix_day=prefix_day)`, and `holiday_name = holiday(date_obj, israel=israel, hebrew=hebrew, prefix_day=prefix_day)`. Set `kind` to 'fast_day' when `fast_name` is not None, otherwise 'festival' when `festival_name` is not None. Return the input date string unchanged as `date`.

tools.name: get_jewish_festival
tools.description: Look up only Jewish festivals for a Gregorian date, with control over working days (Chol Hamoed, Pesach Sheni, etc.) and day-number prefixes.

params.name: date
params.description: Gregorian civil date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

params.name: israel
params.description: Use the Israel festival schedule when true; otherwise use the diaspora schedule.

params.name: hebrew
params.description: Return the festival name in Hebrew letters when true; otherwise return transliterated English.

params.name: include_working_days
params.description: Include festival days on which work is allowed, such as Chol Hamoed and Pesach Sheni.

params.name: prefix_day
params.description: Prefix multi-day festivals with the day number, such as '2 Rosh Hashana'.

returns.name: date
returns.description: The queried Gregorian date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: festival
returns.description: Festival name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a festival.

returns.name: is_festival
returns.description: True if the date is a festival under the selected options.

returns.name: holiday
returns.description: Combined holiday name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a holiday.

returns.name: is_holiday
returns.description: True if the date is a Jewish holiday.

returns.name: fast_day
returns.description: Fast-day name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a fast day.

returns.name: is_fast_day
returns.description: True if the date is a fast day.

tools.implementation_notes: Parse the YYYY-MM-DD string into integers and construct `date_obj = GregorianDate(year, month, day)` from `pyluach.dates`. Import `festival`, `holiday`, and `fast_day` from `pyluach.hebrewcal`. Call `festival_name = festival(date_obj, israel=israel, hebrew=hebrew, include_working_days=include_working_days, prefix_day=prefix_day)`, `holiday_name = holiday(date_obj, israel=israel, hebrew=hebrew, prefix_day=prefix_day)`, and `fast_day_name = fast_day(date_obj, hebrew=hebrew)`. Return those values as `festival`, `holiday`, and `fast_day`, and set each boolean to whether the corresponding value is not None.

tools.name: get_fast_day
tools.description: Look up whether a Gregorian date is a Jewish fast day and return its name.

params.name: date
params.description: Gregorian civil date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

params.name: hebrew
params.description: Return the fast-day name in Hebrew letters when true; otherwise return transliterated English.

returns.name: date
returns.description: The queried Gregorian date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: fast_day
returns.description: Fast-day name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a fast day.

returns.name: is_fast_day
returns.description: True if the date is a fast day.

returns.name: holiday
returns.description: Combined holiday name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a holiday.

returns.name: is_holiday
returns.description: True if the date is a Jewish holiday.

returns.name: festival
returns.description: Festival name in the requested language, or null if the date is not a festival.

returns.name: is_festival
returns.description: True if the date is a festival.

tools.implementation_notes: Parse the YYYY-MM-DD string into integers and construct `date_obj = GregorianDate(year, month, day)` from `pyluach.dates`. Import `fast_day`, `holiday`, and `festival` from `pyluach.hebrewcal`. Call `fast_name = fast_day(date_obj, hebrew=hebrew)`, `holiday_name = holiday(date_obj, israel=False, hebrew=hebrew, prefix_day=False)`, and `festival_name = festival(date_obj, israel=False, hebrew=hebrew, include_working_days=True, prefix_day=False)`. Return those values as `fast_day`, `holiday`, and `festival`, and set each boolean to whether the corresponding value is not None. The library's fast-day lookup has no Israel/diaspora parameter, so related holiday and festival lookups use the diaspora schedule.

tools.name: get_shabbat_for_date
tools.description: Find the Shabbat on or following a Gregorian date, including how many days away it is.

params.name: date
params.description: Gregorian civil date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: date
returns.description: The queried Gregorian date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: shabbat_date
returns.description: Gregorian date of the Shabbat on or following the queried date, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: is_shabbat
returns.description: True if the queried date itself is Shabbat.

returns.name: days_until_shabbat
returns.description: Number of days from the queried date to that Shabbat, where 0 means the queried date is Shabbat.

tools.implementation_notes: Parse the YYYY-MM-DD string into integers and construct `date_obj = GregorianDate(year, month, day)` from `pyluach.dates`. Call `shabbat_obj = date_obj.shabbos()`, which returns a GregorianDate when called on a GregorianDate. Format `shabbat_date` as `f"{shabbat_obj.year:04d}-{shabbat_obj.month:02d}-{shabbat_obj.day:02d}"`. Compute `days_until_shabbat` from the library date objects' subtraction (`shabbat_obj - date_obj`), and set `is_shabbat` to whether that value is 0.

excluded_symbols.reason: Internal helper used for prefix_day formatting; not part of the public agent-facing lookup API.
Internal string-formatting helper behind fast_day; callers should use fast_day instead.
Internal string-formatting helper behind festival; callers should use festival instead.

side_effects: No side effects; all operations are pure in-memory date lookups.
uncertainties: The interface accepts Gregorian civil dates only; Hebrew calendar dates must be converted to Gregorian before calling.
The fast_day lookup has no Israel/diaspora parameter in this library, so fast-day names do not vary by the israel flag.
The combined holiday lookup checks fast days before festivals, so a date that could be interpreted both ways is reported as a fast day.
Name strings depend on the installed pyluach version and its transliteration or Hebrew-letter output.
Invalid YYYY-MM-DD input is expected to raise a normal date-construction error from pyluach.
Shabbat is computed as the Shabbat on or following the queried date, not the preceding Shabbat.
Related holiday and festival lookups from the fast-day tool use the diaspora schedule because that tool has no israel parameter.
